title: A slow service that stops checkout
question: A recommendations service starts taking 30 seconds to answer. Within minutes the checkout, which calls it for a "you may also like" strip, stops responding altogether. What stops this from happening again?
context: Checkout calls recommendations synchronously with the HTTP client's default settings. Its worker pool has 200 threads. Recommendations is not required to complete a purchase.

options.label: Retry the recommendations call up to three times before giving up
options.why: Every retry is another thread held for another 30 seconds and more load on a service that is already struggling. Retries help with brief, independent failures; against a slow dependency they multiply the damage.

options.label: A short timeout and a circuit breaker, rendering checkout without it
options.why: The timeout bounds how long each request can hold a thread; the breaker stops calling once failures pile up, so threads are not spent discovering the same outage; and because the strip is optional, checkout renders without it. The failure stays inside the feature it belongs to.

options.label: Raise the worker pool from 200 threads to 2,000 to absorb the waiting
options.why: The same slow calls fill 2,000 threads, just a little later and with ten times the memory. Capacity does not help when every unit of it is spent waiting on something that will not answer.

options.label: Autoscale checkout on CPU so more instances take up the traffic
options.why: Threads blocked on a slow call use almost no CPU, so the scaler sees idle machines and does nothing — and new instances would block the same way. The resource being exhausted is threads, not processors.
